item.title: Chirihama Nagisa Driveway: Drive Directly on the Beach — Guide
item.description: Chirihama Nagisa Driveway is one of very few beaches in the world where cars can drive directly on the sand, a roughly 8-kilometre stretch of unusually firm, fine-grained beach on the Noto Peninsula’s coast that supports vehicle weight well enough for regular driving. The unusual experience of driving along the open beach with the sea just metres away, waves sometimes lapping close to the tyres, has made it a popular stop for road-trippers exploring the Noto Peninsula, offering photo opportunities and a memorable coastal drive found nowhere else in Japan.

item.title: Noto Peninsula: Rugged Coastlines and Rural Satoyama Landscapes — Guide
item.description: The Noto Peninsula juts into the Sea of Japan from Ishikawa’s northern coast, offering a considerably slower-paced counterpoint to Kanazawa’s city sights, with rugged coastal scenery, traditional fishing villages and terraced rice paddies that helped earn the region UNESCO recognition as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System for its traditional satoyama land management practices. The peninsula’s more remote, less-visited character rewards travellers with time to explore, offering an authentic look at rural coastal Japan increasingly rare elsewhere in the country.

item.title: Noto Satoyama Cycling: Pedalling Through Rural Coastal Ishikawa — Guide
item.description: The Noto Peninsula’s quiet roads, winding between terraced satoyama rice fields, small fishing villages and dramatic coastline, make it a rewarding cycling destination for visitors seeking a slower, less-touristed alternative to Japan’s busier cycling routes. Rental shops in the peninsula’s main towns offer bicycles for day trips or multi-day touring, and the light traffic and varied scenery, from coastal cliffs to inland farmland, give riders a genuine sense of rural Ishikawa’s satoyama landscape at a human pace.

item.title: Wajima Morning Market: One of Japan's Oldest Asaichi — Guide
item.description: Wajima Morning Market, or asaichi, has operated daily for over a thousand years, making it one of Japan’s oldest continuously running street markets, lining a stretch of central Wajima with dozens of small family-run stalls each morning. Vendors, many of them older women who have run the same stall for decades, sell fresh seafood caught along the Noto Peninsula coast, local produce and pickles, alongside Wajima’s famous lacquerware, offering visitors a genuine glimpse of daily life in this coastal fishing town.

item.title: Noto Peninsula Road Trip Guide: Senmaida, Wajima & the Sea of Japan Coast
item.description: The Noto Peninsula extends northward from Kanazawa into the Sea of Japan like a finger pointing toward the Korean coast — a narrow strip of land, roughly 60 kilometres from base to tip, whose distance from any large city has preserved a way of life that has disappeared from most of rural Japan. Here, fishing communities still operate according to seasonal rhythms set centuries ago. Traditional farm families maintain the terraced rice paddies that cascade down hillsides to the sea.
